source_user: Two serving systems claim different tokens/s. Design a reproducible comparison. Scenario variant 219: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: freeze model revision, tokenizer, precision, hardware, topology, prompt/generation distributions, concurrency, warmup, stopping rules, and telemetry; publish raw request traces.
corrected_answer: For variant 219, treat both headline rates as unverified until a shared measurement contract is applied. Define tokens/s separately for input, generated, and accepted tokens per wall-clock second; record request, queue, first-token, token, completion, retry, cancellation, and failure timestamps, and state whether queueing, batching, network, and failed work are included. Freeze and record model and tokenizer revisions, precision, runtime and libraries, drivers, hardware/topology/clocks, serving configuration, decoding and stop rules, prompt and target-length distributions, seeds, concurrency, admission/batching policy, cache state, warmup, test duration, and network path. Replay identical randomized request blocks in paired crossover order at prespecified load levels, with repeated blocks and a fixed stopping rule. Falsifiable hypothesis: admission, batching, or queueing—not decoder execution—is the primary cause of the reported gap; after these controls are equalized, the gap will be below a predeclared practical margin. Measure every token-rate definition, completed requests/s, TTFT, inter-token and end-to-end latency, queue time, p50/p95/p99, errors, timeouts, cancellations, utilization, memory, power/cost, correctness, quality, and telemetry completeness. Publish versioned manifests, seeds, raw per-request traces, and analysis code; report paired effect sizes and confidence intervals. Confounders include workload mismatch, cache warmness, thermal throttling, background load, topology, rate limits, retries, and selective exclusions. Stop or roll back a production canary on error/timeout, correctness, tail-latency, resource, or safety regressions; fail closed and obtain domain review. Do not claim causality if telemetry is incomplete or the margin is not resolved.
risks: Ambiguous token and timing definitions can invalidate comparison.

Missing telemetry or selective exclusions can bias estimates.
evidence_required: Versioned manifests and raw per-request traces for both systems.
Paired repeated results with confidence intervals and the predeclared margin.
Correctness, quality, error, tail-latency, resource, thermal, and telemetry-completeness measurements.
